extra.message: Student.create() builds the SQL INSERT statement by formatting the user-supplied 'name' value directly into the query string using Python's '%' string interpolation, then passes it to cur.execute() with no parameterization. The 'name' value originates from unvalidated POST data (data['name']) in the students() view (views.py:55-57). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL (e.g. name = "x'); DROP TABLE students;--"), allowing full SQL injection.

cwe: CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection')

extra.message: Jinja2 is configured with autoescape=False globally. Combined with templates that render user-controlled data without the '| e' filter, this enables stored/reflected XSS across the application. User-supplied values such as course title/description, student name, and review_text are output raw into HTML.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: review.review_text is rendered without HTML escaping (autoescape is disabled in app.py). The review text is attacker-controlled, persisted via Review.create() from the unauthenticated review() POST handler (views.py:119-129), then displayed to all visitors of the course page. This is a stored XSS: an attacker can submit '<script>...</script>' as review text to run arbitrary JavaScript in other users' browsers.

extra.message: Passwords are verified against an unsalted MD5 hash (md5(password.encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()). MD5 is a fast, cryptographically broken hash and is unsalted here, making stored password hashes trivially crackable via rainbow tables/brute force. A secure password hashing function (bcrypt, scrypt, argon2) with a salt should be used.

cwe: CWE-916: Use of Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort

extra.message: The csrf_middleware is commented out in the middleware list, so CSRF tokens (generated in templates) are never validated for POST requests. State-changing endpoints (login, create student, create course, create review, evaluate, logout) accept cross-site forged requests, allowing CSRF attacks.

The session storage is configured with httponly=False, so the session cookie is accessible to client-side JavaScript. Combined with the XSS vulnerabilities present in this app, an attacker can steal session cookies via script and hijack user sessions.

The students() POST handler creates a new student record from request data with no authentication or authorization check on the server. Access control is only enforced by conditionally hiding the form in the template (for auth_user), but the endpoint itself accepts POST from any unauthenticated client, allowing unauthorized record creation (and is also the SQL injection sink).

The courses() POST handler creates a new course from request data without any server-side authentication or admin check (only the template hides the form behind auth_user.is_admin). Any unauthenticated client can POST to /courses/ to create courses.

The evaluate() handler creates student marks (grades) without any server-side authentication or admin authorization check; only the course.jinja2 template hides the evaluate form behind auth_user.is_admin. Any unauthenticated client can POST to /students/{id}/evaluate/{course_id} to assign grades, a broken access control flaw.

The aiohttp Application is created with debug=True. Running with debug mode enabled in production can expose internal state, verbose error/stack-trace information, and other sensitive details to attackers.

Database credentials (user 'postgres' / password 'postgres') are hardcoded in the configuration file checked into the repository. Hardcoded/committed credentials can be exploited if the repo or config is exposed; secrets should be injected via environment variables or a secrets manager.
